name: Rexism
summary: Rexism was the Belgian movement of Leon Degrelle, which grew out of Catholic Action in the 1930s and sought moral renewal under Church teaching through a corporatist, authoritarian, monarchist order. It opposed liberal democracy, capitalism and Marxism, organised society through family, workplace and nation, and was led by an unconditionally obeyed Chef. After 1936 it radicalised toward fascism, with a conspiracy-driven antisemitism, and under the 1940-44 occupation became openly collaborationist.
scope: The Rexist Party and movement of 1935-1945 led by Degrelle, centred on the Catholic corporatist doctrine of Louis Picard, Jean Denis and Jose Streel and the 1936 electoral campaign; wartime positions (collaboration, Germanic-race claims, Holocaust denial after 1945) are marked as lower confidence where they diverge from the prewar core. Belgium-specific; excludes Flemish nationalist fascism (VNV, Verdinaso). Primary-source coverage is thin: no Rexist programme text could be opened, so the primary source is Pius XI's Quas Primas, the encyclical from which Christus Rex took its name, and doctrine is otherwise reported by reference works.

sources.title: Leon Degrelle
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Attacks on political and financial elites, Greater Belgium, neutrality, one-party views, attacks on Jewish businesses.

sources.title: Quas Primas (encyclical on the Feast of Christ the King)
sources.author: Pope Pius XI
sources.usedFor: The founding Catholic text behind the Christus Rex name: God-derived rulers, Church freedom from the state, critique of secularism.

sources.title: Rexist Party
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Rejection of liberalism, Marxism and capitalism; corporatism, rural and family ideals, and the shift toward open antisemitism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Never a Rexist programme point; inferred from Catholic social-regeneration aims and corporative bodies that would supply social provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages were to be handled through professional corporative bodies rather than statute, and the sources record no wage policy, so no clear lean.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rex rejected liberalism and opposed both capitalism and Marxism, favouring a corporatist order, though it also stressed individual initiative.

public-ownership.rationale: Rex rejected nationalisation as a socialist or communist concept; the state was to supervise, not run industry.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Degrelle's populist attacks on financiers and politically connected bankers suggest sympathy, but no tax programme is documented; inferred.

unions-good.rationale: Corporative trade bodies were to replace class-based organisation; Rex's hostility to class struggle implies distrust of independent unions (inferred).

property-fundamental.rationale: Rex defended private property against socialist nationalisation, while Catholic teaching subordinated it to the common good.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Degrelle attacked collusion between high finance and government and the state was to supervise the economy, so tighter control of big business is plausible; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Sources give no welfare-cutting programme; Catholic social concern pulls one way and anti-statism the other.

worker-ownership.rationale: Rex's corporatism joined employers and workers in shared bodies without transferring ownership; the sources do not discuss worker ownership directly.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Authoritarian and fiercely anti-communist order-minded movement; the sources do not discuss surveillance, so inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Rex's moral-renewal project under Church guidance makes permissiveness unlikely; drugs are never discussed, so inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Rexists themselves produced increasingly vicious antisemitic propaganda and opposed liberal pluralism; inferred as hostile to such limits.

strong-leader.rationale: Members owed unconditional obedience to Degrelle as Chef de Rex, and Rex wanted authoritarian rule in place of parliamentary gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Rex wanted a strong authoritarian state with a supervisory role, the opposite of anarchist rejection of the state.

limit-guns.rationale: An order-and-authority movement would favour state control of arms; not explicitly documented.

empower-police-military.rationale: Rex was authoritarian and strongly anti-communist, and later adopted paramilitary forms; stronger enforcement fits, though budgets are not discussed. The cited sources do not address this directly, so the answer is inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Rexist moral regeneration under Catholic teaching and its retrograde views of women and morality rule this out.

rehabilitation.rationale: Rexist writers like Denis wanted capital punishment even for abortion, implying a punitive outlook; the prison question itself is inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: The family was the foundational natural community and source of social morality in Rexist doctrine, with policy to encourage large families.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Catholic family doctrine with bans on contraception and divorce implies firm opposition; not explicitly addressed in sources.

abortion-legal.rationale: Rexist theorist Jean Denis envisioned capital punishment for women who obtained abortions, according to the Wikipedia account of his writings.

more-religion-public.rationale: Rexism sought moral renewal of Belgium in line with Church teaching and Catholic dominance, rooted in Catholic Action.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The question was anachronistic for Rex; its Belgian nationalism and later racial rhetoric suggest rejection, inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Rex held a separate-spheres view of women as maternal and domestic, with strict sex segregation at work.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Rex was a Belgian nationalist movement stressing the nation as a natural community with family and workplace.

gradual-change.rationale: Rex sought generational moral regeneration and a radical new order via a perpetual movement, not gradual respect for existing institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Nationalist and later antisemitic and xenophobic; immigration policy is not directly documented, so inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalist stance and Degrelle's backing of Belgian neutrality suggest hostility to supranational power; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Rex rejected liberalism and economic order was to be corporative; trade is not discussed, so inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Rex presented itself as Belgian nationalist and the nation was one of three natural communities.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Degrelle backed Belgian neutrality at the start of the war; humanitarian intervention is anachronistic, inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Nationalist, hierarchical movement with an exclusionary turn; open borders contradict its outlook.

limit-growth.rationale: Rex's rural-traditionalist side may be sceptical of industry but no environmental position exists; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate change is anachronistic and unaddressed; no basis to lean either way.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Rexism emphasised moral and spiritual regeneration over technology; no stated position.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Early Rex insisted publicly on pursuing power only through legal, democratic means, though Degrelle later abandoned this.

experts-over-public.rationale: Parliament was to be reduced to ratifying laws drafted by corporative professional bodies, giving expert trade bodies real say.

central-planning.rationale: The state would supervise rather than administer, and nationalisation was rejected; planning by corporative bodies is the nearest option.

socialized-markets.rationale: Rex rejected both socialist public ownership and liberal markets in favour of corporatism; worker ownership is not discussed.

land-value-tax.rationale: Georgist land taxation is not mentioned; Rex's property-protecting corporatism makes it unlikely.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The family as foundational natural community suggests protecting transmission of family property; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Unconditional state income contradicts Rex's duty-based, family-and-corporation social model; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalist corporatists generally favour protected national economies; not specifically documented for Rex.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state would supervise but not administer the economy; whether it directs investment is not stated.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rex idealised rural life and opposed nationalisation and big capital alike, which fits wide small ownership; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nothing suggests Rex wanted anything but a conventional wage economy inside corporative structures.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Degrelle attacked high finance but no monetary-system proposals are recorded; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Rexism organised society through corporative professional bodies representing each trade, with the state supervising them.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rex was a movement under one Chef and in 1941 Degrelle reportedly backed a state without political parties.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Rexism was explicitly monarchist, drawing on Maurras, with the king as unifying national symbol.

democracy-best.rationale: Rex aimed at moral renewal through a corporatist society and the abolition of liberal democracy, though early on it used electoral means.

direct-votes.rationale: Parliament would shrink to ratifying corporative drafts; direct popular lawmaking is at odds with Rex's leader-and-corporation structure.

workers-councils.rationale: Rex opposed Marxism and communism; political power was to rest on corporations, the king and the Chef, not class councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Rex stood for a unitary Belgian identity and rejected the Flemish nationalist alliance over Belgian unity.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rexist doctrine valued hierarchy and the Chef de Rex, and the king alone balanced authority with restraint.

political-violence-never.rationale: Early Rex disavowed illegal means, but it adopted paramilitary forms and Degrelle later requested reprisal killings, so violence was not ruled out.

war-builds-character.rationale: Degrelle volunteered for the Eastern Front and glorified Waffen-SS service, though before 1940 he backed Belgian neutrality.

separate-church-state.rationale: Picard's model treated Church and State as separate but cooperating spheres, not strictly separated, with Church dominance in morals.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Rex wanted law infused with Catholic moral teaching and God-derived authority, though through Church doctrine more than scripture alone.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rex wanted a strong authoritarian state; privatising courts and defence is contrary to its order-based outlook.

military-superiority.rationale: Rex's later militarism and Waffen-SS engagement imply support for strong armed forces; not stated as policy.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Prewar Rex defined the nation as a unitary Belgian community with race largely absent, but from 1943 Degrelle called Walloons Germanic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rex regarded class struggle as the Marxist error and set family, workplace and nation as the harmonious natural communities.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rexism was hierarchical and corporatist, with leaders, trades and sexes in distinct roles.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic for a Belgian nationalist movement; inferred from its nationalism and imperial context.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Belgian-nationalist authoritarians would reject this; Rex's colonial views are not documented, so inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Rex's Catholic outlook and later pan-German turn pull in different directions; no stated position on civilisational unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Rex taught subordination to the collective and moral regeneration, rejecting liberal individualism.

limit-population.rationale: Rexist writers wanted tax and housing policy to encourage large families and bans on contraception.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Rex idealised rural life but sought a corporatist modern economy, not rejection of industry; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Rex stressed restoration of moral order and hierarchy over disruption; technology never addressed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Catholic moral doctrine would reject it; not directly discussed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; Rex placed authority in a Chef, king and corporations.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Authoritarian and order-minded; anachronistic and undocumented, inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Historian Newes-Adeyi calls its gender views more retrograde than new, but Rex also sold itself as national rebirth; its order was largely Catholic and traditional.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Rex presented itself as a quasi-religious movement of moral regeneration, not pragmatic problem-solving.

direct-action.rationale: Rex contested the 1936 election and claimed legal means, but also used marches and rallies; elections were its main route.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses this; Rex's authoritarian methods and its claimed legalism pull apart.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Rex's ideal was a corporatist modern society with a rural moral core, not hunter-gatherer life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Trade-based corporative bodies presuppose separate occupations.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Rex opposed communism and favoured corporative organisation; no stated distribution principle, inferred.

production-for-use.rationale: Rex rejected both capitalism and Marxism; the slogan is a Marxist one, inferred against.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Rex rejected the Marxist class analysis and held employers and workers should cooperate in corporations.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Degrelle styled Rex as strongly anti-communist.

collective-farming.rationale: Rex idealised rural life and opposed communism; collectivisation is the communist model it rejected.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Degrelle blamed Jewish finance and Freemasonry for war rather than capitalism as a system; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Rex favoured a strong authoritarian state and discipline; denying the state's right to tax is incompatible.

harm-principle.rationale: Rex wanted morals enforced for Catholic social order, including bans on divorce and contraception.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rex placed family, workplace and nation as natural communities with duties and subordination to the collective.

conscription.rationale: An authoritarian nationalist movement would accept conscription; not documented directly.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Rex rejected democracy and a market-like exit model; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Rex's Catholic corporatist state was moral and authoritarian, not a customer-service firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Catholic social concern suggests some support, but Rex's materials stress order and duty over liberty; no stated stance.

media-academia-power.rationale: Rex attacked parties, Freemasons and finance, not mainly universities and media; no clear position.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Race was largely absent from prewar Rexism, though later Nazi alignment brought racial doctrines in.

organic-representation.rationale: Rex envisioned representation through family, workplace and nation via corporative professional bodies instead of parliamentary parties.

total-state.rationale: Rex called itself liberal-authoritarian and said the state should supervise rather than administer, leaving room for individual initiative; later radicalisation moved toward Nazi forms.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rex framed itself as a generational, quasi-religious movement for moral regeneration of the nation.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Degrelle pushed for a Greater Belgium at France's and the Netherlands' expense and later a Burgundian state in a pan-German order.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rexist membership meant unconditional personal obedience to Degrelle, resembling oaths of loyalty, but not a feudal lord system.

bound-labor.rationale: Rex idealised rural life but proposed corporations, not legal serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Catholic doctrine holds truth is objective and revealed; relativist claims would be rejected, inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Catholic natural law and divine commandments, as Pius XI stated in Quas Primas, underlay Rex's moral renewal.

single-common-good.rationale: Rex rejected party competition for corporative unity under the Chef and king aiming at one national good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Degrelle blamed Jews for conspiracies; he would not support a Jewish state, though possibly as expulsion; inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not documented; Rex's nationalism and antisemitism suggest rejection.

revive-national-language.rationale: Rex was French-speaking Belgian nationalism and not concerned with reviving lost languages; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Rex favoured corporative cooperation under state supervision, not democratic votes in firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Catholic school interests favour public support for confessional schools; not directly documented.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Sources record no fiscal-policy position beyond attacks on corrupt finance.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rex was liberal-authoritarian but rejected liberalism and held political life above economic liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rexism's moral regeneration and the leader as embodiment suggest moral example mattered, but it also valued authority and punishment.

national-self-determination.rationale: Rex was nationalist, although it opposed Flemish self-determination within Belgium.

force-without-un.rationale: Nationalist movement predating the UN; willingness to use force is inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rex was rooted in Catholic Action and Church teaching with moral renewal under divine authority.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Nationalist exclusivism and later antisemitism suggest benefits for nationals; not documented.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Order, discipline and duty rhetoric suggest agreement; not explicitly addressed.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rex's corporative bodies united employers and workers by trade, replacing class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Rex stressed tradition, Church and monarchy; destroying inherited institutions contradicts this.

dominated-front.rationale: Rex allied with the Axis and was anti-communist; a front against Western powers is not its idea except via Axis collaboration.

workers-nation.rationale: Rex organised workers inside national corporative bodies and rejected international communism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Women could vote but not stand for national office, and were assigned maternal and domestic roles with sex segregation at work.

ban-interest.rationale: Degrelle attacked high finance, and Catholic tradition has anti-usury roots, but no interest ban is documented.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Race was largely absent from prewar Rexist ideology, so segregation law was not a programme item; inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rex saw the state as supervising the nation's natural communities, rejecting Marxist class analysis.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on energy.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationalist unitary-nation ideology suggests assimilation; not documented.

elite-replacement.rationale: Rex's conspiracy theory concerned Judeo-Communist plots and Jewish finance, not demographic replacement; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Rex opposed party-based parliamentary politics in favour of corporative representation.

national-mission.rationale: Rex's nationalism was Belgian-unitary and defensive; a mission to spread its government is not documented.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Rex defended men's and women's distinct spheres as natural, not as a hierarchy to dismantle.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Degrelle's 1936 campaign attacked the corrupt parliamentary elite as the pourris and published scandals about politicians and high finance.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Catholic teaching opposed eugenic sterilisation, and prewar Rex was pronatalist; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: A movement that glorified authority and later collaborated with occupiers would reject this; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rex wanted a state that supervised corporations and enforced morality, not a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Race was largely absent prewar, but later Nazi alignment adopted racial rhetoric; no documented position.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Catholic doctrine affirms equal human dignity, but Rexist hierarchy, sex roles and antisemitism deny equal rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist doctrinal question outside Rex's concern; no stated position.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed; Belgian colonial nationalists would reject it, inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Rex wanted a confessional state, but Belgian Catholics were the majority; no stated position on religious personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: A confessional movement under Church dominance might favour it, but nothing documents this.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: No connection to Catholic Belgian ideology; inferred.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Rexism came from Catholic Action and wanted Church-guided society, so religion in schools was expected.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist doctrine; Rex was anti-communist and sought a strong state on its own terms, inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Picard's vision had political authority derive from God rather than the people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Nationalist corporatists tend towards mercantilism; not documented.

population-transfer.rationale: Rexist militias attacked Jews in 1940 and Rex's hostile conspiracy view of Jews suggests pressure to leave; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Rex joined the Waffen-SS and sought reprisals, rejecting absolute non-aggression.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rex preached harmony among natural communities, though its later Nazi alignment adopted struggle language; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Authoritarian anti-communist movement would ban communists, though Rex itself was banned later; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican liberty is foreign to a movement exalting the Chef and king; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Rex wanted authority concentrated in a king-balanced authoritarian order with parliament merely ratifying.

vanguard-party.rationale: Rex was anti-communist; its own movement-led model resembles a vanguard but for the nation, not the working class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Catholic social teaching stresses care for the poor and Rex promised social regeneration; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Wide small ownership and anti-socialist outlook suggest agreement; not documented.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Corporative class collaboration replaces strikes; no explicit statement on ballot requirements.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Rexist writers wanted incentives for large families, so they would not blame population growth for poverty; the link itself is inferred.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Nationalist unity and later antisemitism suggest agreement; prewar Rex was not explicitly racial.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Hierarchical, leader-centred Rex opposed randomness in offices.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarian and anti-communist; plausible but undocumented.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: No documented position; corporative bodies might set prices but not clearly.

party-controls-media.rationale: Rex wanted an authoritarian order and used propaganda; later imitated SS structure; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Rex was monarchist and the king was the unifying figure; party command of the army is not its model.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: A nationalist movement that tied the nation to natural communities would likely make citizenship hard to gain; the sources never discuss naturalisation.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Rex had no such egalitarian pay demand; inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Rex demanded near-total subordination of members to the collective and unconditional obedience to the Chef.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Degrelle backed neutrality and Belgian unity; supranationalism is anachronistic before the Nazi New Order; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Rex's monarchist model made the king the unifying figure balancing authority.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Rex's Catholic hierarchy-minded outlook assumes episcopal rule, though some bishops opposed Rex.

clerical-rule.rationale: Church and State were distinct cooperating spheres, so clergy did not hold highest political authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Rex was nationalist and rejected Marxist internationalist defeatism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral renewal under Church teaching and bans on contraception and divorce imply moral censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Rex envisioned a king and a Chef, not elected presidents; no stated position.

recall-officials.rationale: Rex opposed democratic accountability in favour of authority and obedience; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Degrelle backed Belgian neutrality at war's start; troops abroad not documented.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing policy favoured large families but no abolition of renting is documented.

people-in-arms.rationale: Rex wanted a disciplined paramilitary order under the Chef, not a popular militia replacing the army; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rexism idealised rural life, hierarchy and traditional family values.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Degrelle's Greater Belgium and pan-German schemes imply support for unifying peoples; inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist attacks on the political class; intellectual elites are not specifically addressed.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nationalist-hierarchical outlook and later Germanic-race claims reject cultural equality.

death-penalty.rationale: Rexist writer Denis envisioned capital punishment even for women who obtained abortions.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Rex's Catholic moral-reform and separate-spheres doctrine reject gender equality teaching.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Catholic Rex was not a creationist movement; no documented position.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Moral renewal in line with Church teaching implies restriction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Rexist nationalism treated the nation as a natural community of family and kin, which fits descent-based citizenship; not directly documented.

minority-language-support.rationale: Rex upheld a unitary Belgian identity against Flemish nationalism.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Confessional Catholic outlook and antisemitism suggest no exemptions for minorities; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Rex demanded subordination to collective and moral conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; Rex had Belgian-nationalist and colonial outlook; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Rex rejected socialist transformation of property; undocumented.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Rex preferred rule by the Chef and corporative bodies over assemblies; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Catholic charity favours aid, nationalism disfavours it; undocumented.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate Rex's active life, and nothing in its nationalism or neutrality stance clearly settles the question.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rexism was explicitly monarchist, wanting the king as unifying national symbol, so it would reject electing the head of state.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Degrelle attacked high-finance influence; independent bankers would draw suspicion; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Greater Belgium irredentism suggests unwillingness to cede land; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Pius XI's Catholic social teaching, which Rex invoked, subordinates property to the common good, though Rex defended property against nationalisation.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Rex saw the USSR as a communist enemy, not state capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk was never a Rexist concern, and the movement's sources give no basis for a lean either way.

collective-defense.rationale: Degrelle backed Belgian neutrality rather than alliance commitments at the start of the war.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Undocumented; Rex's own Greater Belgium ambitions conflict with a general principle.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Quas Primas criticised placing the Church under state control, and Rex's confessional aim was Church-friendly.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The king was to be the unifying national symbol above factions.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Rex insisted on Belgian unity against Flemish nationalism.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Rex's unitary Belgium and Walloon-Flemish stance suggest opposition to special systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Catholic doctrine places authority in God but rejects divine descent of rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The sources record no Rexist tax-structure position; its attacks on high finance and defence of property pull in opposite directions.

character-from-environment.rationale: Catholic view of the soul and moral responsibility implies innate nature matters; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Catholic doctrine binds rulers to God's commandments (Quas Primas); Rex's Chef was bound morally.

space-expansion.rationale: Space was beyond Rex's horizon; its focus on moral and national regeneration gives no basis for a lean.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Monarch plus corporative bodies plus Chef resembles mixed rule in some features; not framed in these terms.

leader-cult.rationale: Members owed unconditional obedience to Degrelle, with mass rallies around the Chef de Rex.

equal-parenting.rationale: Rex's gender-role doctrine favoured maternal domestic roles.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist internal debate; Rex rejects class struggle.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rex rejected socialist property transfers and defended property.

refugee-return.rationale: Rex never addressed refugees' return; its nationalism and its later wartime role pull in different directions.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Degrelle's later pan-German and Greater Belgium claims leaned this way; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Rex was confessional but sources do not record punishing apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Catholic modesty norms but no legal mandate documented.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Degrelle later said Walloons were a Germanic race destined to rejoin the Reich.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Rex favoured unitary Belgium against Flemish autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Rexists' antisemitism leads them to reject Jews' claim to equal membership; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Rex held that moral and spiritual regeneration drives change, rejecting Marxism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporative bodies concentrate trade power, yet Degrelle attacked finance; no documented antitrust stance.

no-bailouts.rationale: Degrelle attacked banker-politicians but no bailout policy is recorded.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rex rejected liberal democracy but also majoritarian parliamentarism; no stated position on courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Women were barred from national office under Rexist doctrine.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The sources show no autarkic programme; corporatism and nationalism suggest some protection but also a Belgian colonial economy.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: International trade agreements with labour and environmental clauses were unknown to Rex, and the sources give nothing to infer a direction.

moral-incentives.rationale: Rex's moral regeneration and duty-before-self orientation fit moral incentives; not stated.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Early Rex pursued legal means and electoral politics.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: A monarchist movement that valued hierarchy and a hereditary king would not abolish titles and privileges.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nationalist movement valuing national tradition; undocumented.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Belgian-nationalist movement of the colonial era; undocumented.

patriotic-education.rationale: Rex's nationalism and youth uniforms point to national loyalty teaching.

public-money-creation.rationale: Degrelle attacked high finance; no monetary reform recorded.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Rex rejected capitalism as a system; no collapse theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Rex's sources do not discuss Belgian cultural influence in the Congo; its colonial-era nationalism offers no clear direction.

delink-world-market.rationale: Undocumented; Rex was a Belgian nationalist with colonial interests.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marxist-Leninist theory rejected by anti-Marxist Rex.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Rex wanted state supervision of the economy and later state discrimination by decree; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rex rejected liberalism and wanted authority and corporative bodies to shape law, so an entrenched rights text limiting government is unlikely; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: The question of colonial-era treaty borders is not addressed in Rexist sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rex favoured a hereditary king and a Chef, rejecting election of rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: A movement demanding unconditional obedience to a leader and subordination to the collective would reject a minority or individual veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Catholic order, obedience and Rex's authoritarianism disfavour resistance; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliament would be reduced largely to ratifying laws drafted by corporative bodies, subordinate to the king and Chef.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Catholic teaching of the period gave animals limited moral weight and Rex's sources never raise the issue.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Catholic social teaching and Rex's hierarchical order include duties of the privileged; undocumented.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Rex demanded committed participation in a perpetually active movement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Rex used mass rallies and propaganda itself and never framed mass culture as a tool of pacification.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory is outside Rexism; Rex's own anti-establishment rhetoric offers no clear lean.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Marxist dependency theory; Rex was anti-Marxist, inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Nationalist exclusivism and later antisemitic measures suggest reserving office for natives, but no Rex source states it.

party-own-road.rationale: This is an internal debate of communist parties and Rex, as an anti-communist movement, never took a position.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development aid was outside Rexist concerns; its nationalism favours self-reliance but its colonial setting complicates it.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Rex became openly aligned with Nazi Germany and its collaboration made anti-fascism its negation.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Rex fought communism but allied with fascism, so it would not condemn both equally.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history never entered Rexist doctrine, so no position can be inferred.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: A traditionalist, nation-and-Church movement would likely defend inherited monuments; not documented.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Rex's gender doctrine had distinct roles; undocumented.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Rex rejected liberal parliamentary democracy for Catholic corporatist institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Authoritarian nationalism and Rex's later paramilitary style suggest a political role for the armed forces, though the king was to balance authority.

paid-care-work.rationale: Rex wanted women in domestic roles and family encouragement but not wages for care work.

filial-duty.rationale: The family was the foundation of society and source of social morality.

office-by-exam.rationale: Rex's corporative bodies chose representatives by trade, and the sources say nothing on civil-service examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nationalism and attacks on finance suggest agreement.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Rexist theorist Jean Denis envisioned a state banning divorce, so ending marriage without fault would be rejected.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Rex rejected delegate democracy in favour of Chef authority.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Rex's corporative social order and Catholic social teaching favour collective trade-based provision over individual private accounts; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Rex idealised rural life and defended property against nationalisation, which conflicts with community-only tenure; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Rex's plan left parliament mainly ratifying budgets and laws.

single-official-language.rationale: Rex was French-speaking Belgian-unitary; undocumented on language law.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Belgian nationalism and attacks on foreign and financial interests suggest restricting foreign ownership; not documented.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Rex's outlook opposes equality-of-outcome doctrines; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Moral regeneration and rural-traditional values suggest agreement; undocumented.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Rex's sources cover no foreign-policy use of insurgents, and its wartime alliance with Germany does not settle it.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bloc discipline was not a Rexist question, though Rex's later alignment with Germany implies acceptance of great-power dominance; no clear lean.

corporate-influence.rationale: Degrelle's campaigns attacked collusion between high finance and government.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Nationalist suspicion of foreign influence suggests agreement, although Rex itself took money from Mussolini and Nazi Germany.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Denis's writings called for tax and housing policy to encourage large families.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchases are a modern question absent from Rexist sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: Corporative bodies were to organise trades, but the sources record no state job guarantee.

democratic-peace.rationale: Rex rejected democracy as the basis of order.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Authority derives from God and members owe unconditional obedience.

non-intervention.rationale: Degrelle backed neutrality, but Rex later served the Reich's expansion.

industrial-unions.rationale: Rex's corporations were organised by trade and profession, not union by industry.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Degrelle blamed Jews and Freemasons for conspiring to push Europe into war, and Rex rhetoric centred on a Judeo-Communist conspiracy.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Family is foundational; Rex wanted bans on divorce and contraception.

public-access-to-information.rationale: An authoritarian movement valuing obedience and Chef-led secrecy is unlikely to support legal access rights; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Rex idealised rural life but proposed no localist production policy.

informal-organisation.rationale: Rex was a disciplined hierarchical movement under a Chef.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Belgian nationalism points to national supremacy, though Rex left no statement on international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Rex's national community was Catholic-shaped through moral renewal, but it nominally upheld a Belgian identity.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: A nationalist movement is unlikely to endorse tributary submission, even though Rex later deferred to Germany in practice.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Rex stood for unitary Belgium and national solidarity against Flemish nationalism, so regional retention is unlikely; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Rex opposed communism and defended private property, so personal belongings would remain private; the commons-for-production half it rejects.

defeat-communism.rationale: USHMM records Degrelle styling Rex as strongly anti-communist.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public service delivery models were outside Rex's concerns; no basis for a lean.

religion-illusion.rationale: Rex arose from Catholic Action and sought Church-guided renewal.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Rex opposed capitalism as well as Marxism; undocumented on progressivity.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Rex defended a maternal and domestic role for women and rejected economic transformation, so it would deny the link.

socialized-care.rationale: Rexism made family and mothers the core of domestic care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Rex's sources show no concern with language purification; its French-speaking Belgian nationalism gives no clear lean.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not part of the Belgian Rexist context.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Rex's model was a unified nation with corporations.

majority-settlement.rationale: Planned settlement of majorities in minority areas was not a Rexist programme.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rex opposed both Marxism and capitalism while favouring corporatism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Rex's Greater Belgium ambitions suggest historical claims, but its sources do not frame this as a general principle.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Degrelle after the war denied the Holocaust; though not a Rexist era doctrine, this was the movement's leader's postwar stance.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Catholic moral renewal and Rex's conservative morality suggest criminal sanction, but no source records it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Rex became more openly antidemocratic and Degrelle backed a partyless state.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: A movement aiming at Catholic dominance in morals would plausibly punish blasphemy; not documented.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Belgian colonial-era nationalism accepted metropolitan benefit as the colonies' purpose; Rex's own colonial doctrine is not documented.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic doctrine foreign to Catholic Belgian Rexism, which has no reason to endorse it; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; Church-state were separate spheres.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Rex rejected democratic participation for Chef rule.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Rex denied class struggle and held gender roles natural.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Rex's separate-spheres doctrine and Catholic morality would reject legal recognition of gender identity; the issue is anachronistic, so inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Catholic doctrine on the sanctity of life, which Rex followed through its harsh stance on abortion, rejects assisted dying; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Rex claimed to transcend both and be neither capitalist nor Marxist.

alienated-labor.rationale: This is a Marxist concept that Rex, as an anti-Marxist corporatist, would reject as a diagnosis of capitalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: A Catholic nationalist movement would probably see Islam as foreign to national culture; not documented, inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Louis Picard's vision, which shaped early Rex, held political authority derives from God rather than the people.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Catholic confessional movement would not ban religious dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic employment-law issue that Rex's sources never touch.

social-market-economy.rationale: Corporatist, not exactly social market; undocumented.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Rex became paramilitary and Degrelle later joined the Waffen-SS, and its order-minded authoritarianism would never abolish armies.

rich-first.rationale: Neither Rex's corporatist rhetoric nor its anti-finance populism clearly endorses or rejects letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Degrelle supported Belgian neutrality at the start of the war.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Rex was explicitly monarchist, so hereditary succession from parent to child fits its model of the king.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Degrelle attacked high finance, but no Rexist source proposes mutual credit banking.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF-style conditions are anachronistic for Rex and nothing in its sources bears on them.

property-franchise.rationale: Women could vote under Rex's plan; no property qualification documented.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Rex defended separate spheres for women and men, so it would reject ecofeminist claims; the ecological side is inferred.

reification.rationale: This Marxist concept is outside Rexist doctrine, which rejected Marxist analysis of capitalism.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Degrelle attacked politicians' ties to finance; no press doctrine.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: A Chef-led authoritarian movement with unconditional obedience favours leader discretion over rule by fixed laws; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Race was largely absent prewar and women could vote.

online-participation.rationale: Digital participation is anachronistic and Rex favoured leader and corporative authority over mass deliberation.

open-government-data.rationale: An authoritarian movement demanding obedience is unlikely to favour open publication of decision records; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Catholic confessional doctrine and Rex's hostility to Jews suggest favouring such restrictions; no source documents a Rexist law.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Random citizen assemblies contradict Rex's hierarchical, Chef-and-corporation model; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Rex was rooted in traditional Catholic teaching under Pius XI's Quas Primas and rejected modernising reinterpretation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Degrelle attacked the power of high finance over government, but liberty as such was not Rex's main value.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Rex's Catholic morality and militarist, hierarchical order make open service unlikely; the issue is anachronistic, so inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Rexism grew out of Catholic Action and sought Church-guided moral renewal, so promoting atheism is the opposite.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: An authoritarian order-minded movement favouring capital punishment would reject abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Rex insisted on a unitary Belgium against Flemish nationalism, so it would resist formal community power-sharing; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Catholic subsidiarity favours church charities and local communities, though Rex's state supervised society; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Rex envisioned a king and a permanent Chef, not elected politicians in terms; no clear lean.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid delegation conflicts with Rex's hierarchy and corporative representation; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is anachronistic for Rex and absent from its sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Rexist doctrine kept women to maternal and domestic roles and Catholic practice reserves the priesthood to men.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Rex made the family a hierarchical foundation with a maternal role for women, suggesting male headship; no source states it.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Rex's nationalism and its limit on women standing for office show a narrow view of who takes part in politics; inferred for foreigners.

rent-control.rationale: Housing markets were not a Rexist concern beyond family-oriented housing policy.

abolish-ip.rationale: Rex defended private property and attacked socialism; abolishing patents and copyrights fits neither; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Rex adopted paramilitary uniforms and generational youth rhetoric.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is anachronistic for Rex and its sources give no basis for a lean.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Rex wartime collaboration with persecution of Jews; undocumented.

decide-locally.rationale: Rex insisted on a unitary Belgian identity and rejected Flemish regionalism, though its natural-community and trade-body model gives local bodies some place; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Members owed near-total subordination to the collective and unconditional obedience to the Chef, and the family and nation came before the individual.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Catholic doctrine treats creation as God's work but Rex's sources never address nature or the environment; no clear lean.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from a movement that glorified combative leadership and armed struggle against Marxism rather than any pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not stated; inferred from Rexist Belgian nationalism and appeals to a Burgundian and Catholic national past.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the Catholic traditionalist family doctrine, which treats sex roles as natural.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from a doctrine that organised society through family and assigned women a domestic role.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not documented as doctrine; inferred from the leader cult and sacralised, combative style of the movement.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Christus Rex framed politics as a Catholic crusade of moral renewal against Marxism and liberal decadence, drawing on Quas Primas.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not stated; inferred from Degrelle's Greater Belgium aims, which saw the homeland as a state to expand and gather people.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not stated; Rex sought state power for a moral order, so culture first is inferred to be a poor fit.

god-not-male.rationale: Quas Primas and the Rexist Catholic doctrine speak of God and Christ the King in traditional male terms; no revision was sought.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Rexism took Church teaching as authoritative and a fixed standard; a test based on women's humanity is contrary to it.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Degrelle attacked Jewish businesses and financial elites, implying economic life belonged in the hands of the national majority.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; Rex sought a unitary corporatist Belgium but also Greater Belgium annexations, so no clear answer on merging regions can be inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Corporatism folds workers and employers into state-recognised corporations under an authoritarian Chef, leaving no room for unions independent of the ruling order.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Rexism rejected Marxism and class politics in favour of class collaboration; inferred from that, adherents would not tie socialism to working-class power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from corporatist doctrine, which sought functional representation of occupational bodies beside or in place of a purely party-elected parliament.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from Rexism's defence of private property within a corporative order, with no communal ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the centralised, unconditionally obeyed Chef and the Greater Belgium aim; delegate-only confederations with assembly rule run against that.

family-wage.rationale: Catholic social doctrine placed the family at the base of the order and Rexism organised society through family, workplace and nation, which fits a family-supporting wage.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian state's wish to control and monitor; no Rexist statement on money exists.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian, one-party outlook; no Rexist statement on communications exists.

person-over-state.rationale: Rexism put the nation and the Chef's order above the individual, though its Catholic roots pull the other way; inferred from the authoritarian structure.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Rexism sought moral and spiritual renewal under Church teaching, drawing its name from Christ the King as in Quas Primas.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from unitary Belgian nationalism and a strong central Chef, so regional powers would be revocable.

gm-crops.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Not a point of this ideology; no position is inferable from its sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Prewar Rexism was not racial (it was Catholic and national) while its wartime phase claimed Germanic-race ties, so adherents are split.

racial-pride.rationale: Wartime Rexism stressed Germanic racial kinship and Degrelle took pride in it; the prewar core was national and Catholic rather than racial.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Degrelle advocated Belgian neutrality before the war, which implies armed forces for defence only, though the later Waffen-SS service contradicts it.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Degrelle's Rexism was Belgian and Greater Belgian in outlook, tied to Catholic and monarchist loyalty and Walloon-Belgian unity, and it later turned to Germanic-race claims, so shared language alone was not the criterion.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: Rexism rejected parliamentary party democracy for corporatist representation by family, workplace and nation, not by separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Rexism stressed internal conspiracies of financial and political elites and Jews; a foreign plot to partition Belgium is not documented, though some adherents backed Belgian neutrality against such pressure.

free-public-college.rationale: Not an issue in Rexist doctrine; Catholic school freedom mattered more than state tuition, so no clear lean can be inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: a Catholic corporatist movement that rejected liberal capitalism had no environmental doctrine and would not rely on market taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from Catholic family and rural-order ideals that stress duty to descendants; environmental stewardship is not stated.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Rexism held a Catholic view of women centred on family and motherhood, which values a distinct role but does not argue for giving women's values more weight in politics.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred: an authoritarian, nationalist movement that ended up collaborating with Germany and raising Waffen-SS units was not disarmament-minded, though it backed neutrality before the war.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from authoritarian leader-rule and rejection of parliamentary scrutiny; the question was not addressed.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from Rexist attacks on financial elites and banks and its corporatist rejection of liberal capitalism, though no concrete capital-control policy is documented.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: it championed an authoritarian state with order and discipline, but it also ran its own uniformed formations.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: it prized order and obedience to the Chef and nation, so it would reject refusal, though prewar Rex stressed Belgian neutrality.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Rexism wanted class struggle replaced by corporatist, state-organised occupational bodies rather than free bargaining between unions and employers.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; it attacked parliamentary and financial corruption but proposed no legal fiscal rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: a Catholic-corporatist, nation-focused movement of the 1930s had no developing-country agenda.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Inferred: it attacked parliamentary democracy and party politics ('clean sweep') but aimed to replace them with a corporatist, authoritarian state it would run.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: it prescribed a single corporatist blueprint for the economy under Christ-the-King Catholic principles.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: Rexism joined Catholic faith to national renewal and wartime Germanic claims, but its first loyalty was to Christ the King, with the nation second.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: it backed Belgian national unity and opposed Flemish and Walloon regionalism.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Its Catholic doctrine, as in Quas Primas and Church teaching, grounds human dignity in a created nature, though it did not grant universal liberal rights.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: it used its own press (Rex publishing) as a propaganda arm and wanted media under moral and state direction rather than independent.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Quas Primas, the source of the Christus Rex name, presents Christ's kingship as binding on rulers and nations, which implies one true religion; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: The movement idealised rural and family life and corporative organisation, which implies protection for farmers.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear arms are anachronistic for the 1930s movement, and its neutralist, Greater Belgium views give nothing clear to infer from.

workers-own-party.rationale: Rexism rejected Marxism and liberalism and organised workers in corporative bodies with employers, not in independent class parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from its Catholic moral-order doctrine.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Catholic traditionalism and a limited public role for women point one way, but the sources do not mention inheritance rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Rexism was a unitary Belgian movement and the sources do not address regional language naming.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Its corporatist, authoritarian state would set rules centrally rather than leave pollution to private suits; inferred, pollution is not discussed.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Authority was to rest in the Chef, the monarchy and corporative bodies, with no place for customary chiefs, a concept foreign to Belgium; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmental policy is not addressed and nothing in the sources allows an inference.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Its authoritarian, anti-liberal order favours firm, fixed punishment; inferred, as sentencing is not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: A nationalist movement stressing national unity would likely expect immigrants to adopt the national language; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from a corporatist plan that organises workers and employers in professional bodies set by the state rather than voluntary union membership.

voter-id.rationale: Rexism opposed parliamentary democracy and the sources record no electoral-roll policy.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Rex took its name from Christ the King and sought a social order under Catholic teaching, which gives one church precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Rexism opposed liberal democracy and favoured an authoritarian order under an unconditionally obeyed leader.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from Catholic Action origins and moral-renewal aims; sexual morality is not stated in the sources.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from an authoritarian outlook that subordinates liberties to order; the movement predates the internet.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from corporatism, which deals with welfare through professional bodies and not through cash transfers.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from Catholic corporatist ideas of the family as the unit of society; Belgian women had no national vote in the 1930s and the sources are silent.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: As a Catholic movement it holds that the Church protects women's dignity, so it rejects the claim; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Wartime Rexism adopted Germanic-race claims, which treat race as real, though the prewar core did not address it.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from Catholic corporatist views of the family and women's place; the movement predates equality agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred: corporatist, Catholic social order places property under family and corporate duties; first-claim ownership is not a Rexist theme.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from Degrelle's nationalism and neutrality stance and hostility to elites; international trials of leaders never discussed.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred: Catholic doctrine of Quas Primas treats scripture as divine, but Catholic teaching is not strictly literalist and Rexism does not address it.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: Rexism put women in the family role and opposed equality-from-the-outset guarantees; the group-self-rule framing was not addressed.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Rexism was founded on anti-communism and hostility to Marxism, so a Marxist planned state is not defended.

indirect-election.rationale: Rexist corporatism organised society through family, workplace and nation bodies with an authoritarian head rather than direct universal elections.

national-church-status.rationale: Quas Primas, the source of the Christus Rex name, calls for the state to acknowledge the Church and Christ's kingship; Catholic primacy in Belgium follows.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: Degrelle favoured a unified Greater Belgium and opposed Flemish nationalism, so ethnic territorial autonomy is rejected.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: a single leader-led nation state decides territorial questions; plebiscites are not part of the doctrine.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred: Belgian-nationalist emphasis on territorial integrity and order favours keeping inherited borders; colonial independence was not addressed.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the rural and family ideals attributed to Rexism; no explicit simple-living programme.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: a unitary Belgian nationalism rejects special regional carve-outs; the question is anachronistic for Belgium.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic family and gender-role teaching of Rexism that conscription stays male-only.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from Rexism's Catholic nationalism and moral-renewal aim; Belgian land is not its theme in the sources.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred as indifferent: the sources show authoritarianism but nothing on drug policy.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic for the 1930s movement and never addressed by the sources.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Rexism was Belgian-centred; wartime Germanic claims aside, the sources show no kin-minority program.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the corporatist order and hostility to capitalism, which put resources under organised bodies rather than equal individual claims.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic rejection of liberal individualism in favour of family, work and nation.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Taxation is not discussed in the sources.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from corporative social provision; the targeting question is never addressed.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Rexism attacked the parliamentary party system and demanded unconditional obedience to the Chef.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the 1936 campaign against corrupt politicians and bankers; privileges for business are not discussed directly.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Rexism sought a state ordered by Church teaching and Christ the King, so religion shapes politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Catholic traditionalism and modern corporatism pull in different directions.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Rexist theorist Jean Denis envisioned banning contraception and divorce, and Catholic doctrine reinforces this.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the national corporatist aim; resource ownership is not discussed.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Never addressed as such; inferred from its rejection of capitalism and its corporatist, Catholic social order, which judged distribution by moral and social ends rather than by free exchange.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not a Rexist programme point; inferred from Degrelle's attacks on financial and political elites and the movement's anti-capitalism.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Anachronistic and never discussed; inferred from a racialised, antisemitic nationalism that did not treat racism as a barrier to be removed.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Adherents were split in principle: Catholic natural-law thinking sets justice above positive law, while the movement demanded unconditional obedience to the Chef and the state it would build.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from a corporatist, family-centred order that valued work within workplace and nation rather than an automated economy.

multipolar-world.rationale: Prewar Rex stressed Belgian neutrality and a Greater Belgium, while wartime Rex accepted a German-dominated Europe, so the answer is split and inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from the movement's anti-Marxism and its Catholic corporatism, which treated capital and labour as partners rather than as sources of exploited value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from a nationalist corporatism that organised workers through family, workplace and nation; solidarity with workers abroad was not part of it.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from a Catholic movement of moral and spiritual renewal under Christ the King, which put moral order ahead of purely material interests.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Rex opposed both communism and liberal capitalism, so a communist party directing a market economy was something it rejected on both counts.

missingStatements.text: Contraception and divorce should be prohibited by law.
missingStatements.rationale: Rexist theorist Jean Denis envisioned a state that would ban contraception and divorce and punish abortion.

notes: Prewar Rex (1935-37) was a Catholic corporatist movement claiming legal means; after 1937 it radicalised, adopting antisemitism and, under occupation, collaboration. Racial and expansionist answers are lower confidence because race was largely absent before 1939 and the Germanic-Walloon claims came late. The Holocaust-denial answer reflects Degrelle's postwar stance, not a Rexist-era doctrine.
